In reactions 1 and 2, X represents an element in Period 3.
In each reaction, X is forming a product where X is in its highest oxidation state.
reaction 1
chlorine + element X →XyClz
reaction 2
oxygen + element X →XₚOq
Which ratios show a steady increase from sodium to phosphorus?
neither z:y nor q:p

Sodium, magnesium, aluminium, silicon and phosphorus are all elements in Period 3 of the Periodic
Table.
Three statements about the oxides and chlorides of these elements are given.
The ionically bonded oxides all react with dilute hydrochloric acid.
1
All metal chlorides produce neutral solutions when added to water.
2
The two most electronegative elements both form covalently bonded chlorides.
3
Which statements are correct?
2 and 3 only

solutions are measured.
The same two elements are reacted separately with an excess of chlorine to form their chlorides.
Each chloride is then added separately to water and the pH values of the resulting solutions are
measured.
Which row is correct?
chloride giving
the higher pH
oxide giving
the higher pH
magnesium

Bromocresol green is an acid-base indicator. Below a pH of 3.8 it is yellow. Above a pH of 5.4 it is
blue. Between these values it is green.
Bromocresol green is added to the aqueous solution formed when the chloride of element T is
added to water. The colour becomes yellow.
When an excess of the solid oxide of element U is slowly added to this yellow solution, the indicator
turns green then blue.
Which row could identify element T and element U?
element U
element T

silicon

options.B: 1.0g of phosphorus oxide and 1.0g of phosphorus chloride

Elements Y and Z are both in Period 3 of the Periodic Table.
When the chloride of element Y is added to water, it reacts and a solution of pH 2 is produced.
When the chloride of element Z is added to water, it dissolves and a solution of pH 7 is produced.

options.B: Element Y is magnesium and element Z is sodium.
options.C: Element Y is phosphorus and element Z is aluminium.
options.D: Element Y is silicon and element Z is sodium.
